skill.name: triaging-issues
skill.description: GitHub issue triage support for classifying issues, finding duplicates, mapping relationships, and reviewing issue quality.
skill.summary: Triage GitHub issues with duplicate checks, relationship mapping, quality review, and practical next steps.

security_audit.summary: I found no malicious intent, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or arbitrary command execution in the reviewed files. Static alerts come from expected GitHub CLI helper scripts, jq pipelines, /dev/null redirections, and Markdown code fences. The scripts can change GitHub issues and projects when run, so users should review commands before bulk actions.

remediation.suggestion: Add explicit dry-run and confirmation flags to label, close, and project-update helpers before making changes.
Validate issue numbers, day counts, labels, and project numbers before passing them to gh or date.

content.value_statement: GitHub issue queues become hard to manage when duplicates, stale reports, and missing details accumulate. This skill guides structured triage, duplicate checks, relationship mapping, and issue-quality reviews.
actual_capabilities: Classifies issues by type, priority, scope, and effort using a documented workflow.
Finds possible duplicate issues with GitHub CLI search helper scripts.
Maps mentioned, blocking, and related issues for planning decisions.
Suggests labels, assignments, project placement, and duplicate-resolution actions.
Reviews issue quality for title, body, labels, reproduction steps, and environment details.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI authentication and repository permissions.
Duplicate detection is mostly keyword based and may miss semantic matches.
Bulk helper scripts can edit or close GitHub issues when executed.
The skill does not verify that labels, teams, or project boards exist.

use_cases.title: Daily Issue Intake
use_cases.description: Review new issues, assign labels, identify missing details, and route important work quickly.

use_cases.title: Duplicate Cleanup
use_cases.description: Find similar reports, choose the canonical issue, and prepare respectful closure comments.

use_cases.title: Release Planning
use_cases.description: Map blockers and related issues so teams can choose the next feasible work.

prompt_templates.title: Triage One Issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a single GitHub issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Triage issue #42. Classify it, identify missing information, check likely duplicates, and suggest labels without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Triage Queue
prompt_templates.scenario: Review several open issues that need attention.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review open issues with the needs-triage label. Summarize categories, priorities, duplicates, and recommended next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Map Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze issues #42, #43, and #45. Show blockers, related issues, and a recommended implementation order.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Weekly Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced report for maintainers and project leads.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a weekly triage report for open bugs. Include stale issues, high-priority items, duplicate groups, and project-board recommendations.

output: Classification: bug, high priority, backend scope.
Quality: clear title and reproduction steps, but missing server logs.
Recommendation: add bug and priority labels, request logs, and link related authentication issues.

output_examples.input: Find duplicate issues for the authentication error report.
output: Possible duplicate: issue #38 has the same error code and affected component.
Related but separate: issue #27 describes a timeout with a different root cause.
Recommendation: keep issue #38 as canonical and link the newer report.

output_examples.input: What can the team work on next?
output: Ready: issue #42 has no blockers and unblocks profile and password-reset work.
Blocked: issues #43 and #45 depend on authentication work.
Recommendation: start issue #42 first, then schedule dependent issues after completion.

best_practices: Review suggested labels, closures, and project updates before applying changes.
Keep a canonical issue for each duplicate group and link all related reports.
Ask for missing reproduction details before closing unclear bug reports.
anti_patterns: Do not close issues as duplicates based only on a similar title.
Do not run bulk edits without checking the matched issue list first.
Do not assign priority without considering user impact and urgency.

faq.question: Does this skill change GitHub issues automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest or run helper scripts that change issues. Review actions before executing bulk updates.

faq.question: What tools does it require?
faq.answer: It expects the GitHub CLI and jq for helper scripts. Some workflows also use Python.

faq.question: Can it detect every duplicate?
faq.answer: No. The provided scripts use keyword and title matching, so manual review remains important.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it useful for small repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It can still standardize labels, priorities, and issue-quality checks.

faq.question: Can it create a dependency graph?
faq.answer: Yes. The relationship mapper can summarize issue references and output a graph-friendly format.
